messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] PROD /v1/generate: error-rate spike > 8% (5xx + gateway timeouts) across us-west-2. Paging oncall @dana.

incident-bot: Affected pods: runtime-scheduler-{a,b,c} and gateway-{x,y}. Latency p95 increased from 230ms -> 1.4s. Queue length for batching_scheduler queue avg 18k, HOL stalls observed.

dana: on it. grabbing logs and current autoscale state. tagging @sam and @maya.

sam: I see a wave of batched requests with long tails, looks like one model shard overloaded. running `kubectl get hpa -n prod` and `curl` on scheduler admin.

sam: scheduler queue depth: 
```
queue_name: batching_scheduler
workers: 12
pending_items: 18432
avg_wait_ms: 3200
head_of_line_blocked: true
```

maya: thanks. looks like continuous batching + large request sizes from a few customers causing head-of-line blocking. The runtime KV cache hit-rate is low for these flows. Could be recent client change or bursty traffic.

dana: putting emergency mitigation plan: 1) apply gateway-level short-circuit for small requests (bypass batching) 2) throttle heavy requesters by ip/tenant 3) scale scheduler pool + restart overloaded shard 4) enable per-route circuit-breaker -> fallback model.

jeff: flagged top affected customers in support queue. One Dedicated customer is reporting timeouts. sending them note: "we see elevated 5xx/timeouts; mitigation in progress, will DM with ETA."

sam: running quick actions: increasing scheduler replicas from 12->20 (scale up), and bumping worker concurrency. executing:
```
kubectl scale deployment/runtime-scheduler -n prod --replicas=20
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/scheduler/redispatch?force=true
```

maya: while scaling completes, enable gateway rate limiting for heavy tenants and set batching window to 10ms (was 50ms) to reduce large batch formation. Applying patch to gateway config now.

dana: applied gateway config change: `batch_window_ms=10` and added tenant-level token bucket: `rate=200req/s, burst=50` for tenant ids: [T-873, T-402].

sam: restart triggered for runtime-scheduler shard-b. logs show backlog draining slowly; still seeing 502s from scheduler-proxy -> model-host on shard-c.

maya: deploying hotfix to scheduler: small change to dequeue logic to prefer small requests (preemptive scheduling). rolling canary to shard-a first. config diff:
```
- pop_oldest()
+ pop_prefer_small_jobs()
```

dana: canary healthy on shard-a (10m). promoting to remaining replicas.

sam: after promotions, pending_items down from 18k -> 3.2k over 8 minutes. p95 latency improving to ~380ms. error-rate dropping to 1.6%.

jeff: support update sent to affected customers; one reported immediate improvement. still monitoring for retries impacting downstream.

leo: any customer-facing note we should publish? want to be proactive for Dedicated customers.

dana: yes — short status: "We experienced elevated errors/timeouts due to scheduler batching saturation. We applied targeted gateway throttles, shortened batching window, scaled scheduler, and deployed a prioritization hotfix. Service is recovering; we'll follow up with postmortem and mitigation to avoid recurrence"

sam: creating an incident ticket with root-cause indicators (large batch sizes from small-number of tenants + KV cache misses + scheduling preemption bug). tagging for postmortem: @maya for runtime fix, @sam for autoscale config, @dana for customer comms.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged and assigned to dana (primary). Next oncall sam in 45m for handoff.

dana: handing off to sam at +45. leaving notes: current state: error-rate 1.1%, pending_items 870, all shards healthy, fallback routing enabled for model-variants.

sam: got it. will monitor next 2 hours and run long-tail query to ensure KV cache warms: `histogram(kv_cache_hit_rate, 5m)`.

maya: follow-ups: 1) add tenant-based early-shed policy to gateway, 2) increase autoscale aggressiveness for scheduler, 3) add metric alert for batch-window spikes > 100ms.

dana: thanks all. moving thread to incidents/postmortems for a writeup once we capture logs and timeline.

incident-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Severity -> S2 (customer-impacting, partial). Postmortem scheduled in 24h."
